_meta.angleConvention: Sagittal included angle between segments, 180 = straight, smaller = more flexed; carpus exceeds 180 (hyperextension) in stance. Shoulder=scapula-humerus, elbow=humerus-antebrachium, carpus=antebrachium-metacarpus, hip=pelvis-femur, stifle=femur-tibia, tarsus=tibia-metatarsus.
_meta.phaseConvention: Fraction of stride at which each foot touches down, relative to left hind (LH) touchdown = 0.
_meta.confidence: A = abstract-level number with clear definition; B = peer-reviewed but definition/convention unclear or second-hand; C = popular/garbled; EST = Firefly synthesis, not a measurement.
_meta.caveat: Publisher sites were blocked; nearly all numbers come from web-search snippets of the cited papers, not full texts.

walk.phaseSource: maes2008: canonical PL=75 (LF at 0.25) and measured PL=84+-5% (LF at ~0.16); LH->LF = 1-PL. Conf A/B.

dutyFactor.source: Rule DF>0.5, fore>hind (maes2008); canonical model 0.75 (Cartmill 2002). No measured dog walk DF retrieved.

bodyBuild.note: Long-legged dogs: lateral-couplet tendency (LF 0.05-0.20 after LH); short-legged: single-foot (~0.25).

trot.type: diagonal 2-beat, short or no suspension at slow speed
trot.phaseSource: maes2008 FL=HL=PL=50 (A). Small hind-before-fore lag (0-0.03) is EST; Bertram 2000 notes hind/fore contact timing differs by breed.

dutyFactor.source: labTrotST (Labrador ST% thoracic 43.5, pelvic 36.7); DF falls with speed 2-5 m/s

trot.speedUp: mainly longer strides; elbow and hip ROM grow with speed (weimaraner)

carpus.note: value, SD; hyperextended >180 from just before touchdown through stance

tarsus.note: value, SD; flex-extend in both stance and swing

curveShapes.shoulder: max extension at touchdown, slowly flexes through stance, rapid flexion to peak mid-swing (malinois)
curveShapes.elbow: extends through stance to max at toe-off, flexes to peak mid-swing (rohwedderElbow)
curveShapes.carpus: hyperextends early stance, holds to toe-off, max flexion mid-swing (malinois; gsdCushion2026)
curveShapes.tarsus: yields (flexes) after touchdown then extends to push off; flexes again in swing (gsdCushion2026)

body.spine: 2 flexion-extension cycles per stride, 1 lateral bend + 1 axial rotation cycle
body.neck: lateral translation smaller than at walk

pace.type: lateral pairs together; some long-legged dogs, fast walk/slow run

transverseGallop.type: asymmetric; hind pair then contralateral fore then ipsilateral fore; one flight
transverseGallop.sequenceExample: LH (trail hind), RH (lead hind), LF (trail fore), RF (lead fore)
transverseGallop.phaseSource: LF from Maes PL=73.9+-6.8% (A); within-pair lags ~0.10-0.12 are EST

modelPhases_Ding2025.note: prescribed evenly spaced in a SLIP model, not measured

rotaryGallop.type: asymmetric; trailing fore, lead fore, flight, trailing hind, lead hind (lead hind on opposite side); dogs show double suspension at speed
rotaryGallop.sequenceExample: RH (trail hind), LH (lead hind), LF (trail fore), RF (lead fore)
rotaryGallop.phaseSource: LH->LF = 1 - PL(70.3+-8.3%) from maes2008 (A); within-pair lags ~0.10 EST

dutyFactor.note: derived: stance 72-77 ms at about 3.3-3.5 Hz; Hudson's 131-143 ms at 9 m/s would give about 0.45, which conflicts

body.spine: largest bending in lumbar; flexion about 2x extension; flex with hinds down, extend to reach fores, flex to bring hinds forward
body.tail: held stable by co-contraction of all tail muscles

anatolianShepherd.note: carpus value suspicious (standing carpus normally ~180-195); convention may differ

gsdVsLab_flexionFromStraight.note: 0 = straight convention; included approx = 180 - value for stifle/hock

labradorGoniometry_unverified.source: Jaegger, Marcellin-Little & Levine 2002 AJVR (from memory, NOT verified this session)

northernBreeds.note: lowest cost of transport (3.0 J/kg/m total), broad trot speed range; best model for wolf/dingo-like dogs

wolf.source: popular sources (Wikipedia: Hunting behavior of gray wolves)
